Theme

Latin word

dum

conjunction, with the indicative · Wiktionary

as long as, while; provided that, as long as; provided that, so long as; until; while

In this lexicon

  • as long as

    also used · classical · Plaut. Persa 113: Dum māne est, omnīs ēsse mortālīs decet.; Ov. Met. 2.89: dum rēsque sinit, tua corrige vōta

  • as long as

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.97: ōderint, dum metuant (Accius, quoted by Cicero; Lewis & Short); Cato Agr. 5.4: id faciat saepe, dum nē lassus fīat

  • condition

    also used · classical · Accius in Cic. Off. 1.97: ōderint, dum metuant; Cic. Brut. 285: dummodo sit polīta (Lewis & Short)

  • until

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.78: dum dēfervēscat īra; Lewis & Short s.v. dum

  • while

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 7.8: hominēs, dum docent, discunt; Hor. S. 1.5.71–72: paene … ārsit dum turdōs versat in ignī; Traupman 406

Examples

  • Dum māne est, omnīs ēsse mortālīs decet.

    As long as it is morning, every mortal ought to eat.Plaut. Persa 113

    In the entry for as long as

  • nāte, cavē, dum rēsque sinit, tua corrige vōta

    take care, my son, and change your wish while there is still timeOv. Met. 2.89

    In the entry for as long as

  • ōderint, dum metuant

    let them hate, as long as they fearCic. Off. 1.97 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for as long as

  • opus rūsticum omne cūret utī sciat facere, et id faciat saepe, dum nē lassus fīat

    let him make sure he knows how to do every job on the farm, and do it often, as long as he doesn’t tire himselfCato Agr. 5.4

    In the entry for as long as

  • dum dēfervēscat īra

    until the anger cools downCic. Tusc. 4.78

    In the entry for until

    take the road until you reach the river’s sourceOv. Met. 11.139

    In the entry for until

  • movērī vetuisse puerum dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset

    she forbade anyone to move the boy until he woke up by himselfLiv. 1.39.2

    In the entry for until

  • ūsque adeō, dōnec cremor crassus erit factus

    (stir) until the gruel has become thickCato Agr. 86

    In the entry for until

  • mūtuō ista fīunt, et hominēs, dum docent, discunt

    it works both ways: people learn while they teachSen. Ep. 7.8

    In the entry for while

  • dum differtur vīta trānscurrit

    while it is put off, life runs pastSen. Ep. 1.2

    In the entry for while
